I lived North of Homer, Alaska for three years. In the summer the sun would sort of slide up in the NorthEast and circle around. It would go down (for us) behind Mount Illiamna, back out and behind Mount Redoubt and then stay just below the horizon till sunrise. In the Winter it would come up across Kachemak Bay from Homer going almost straight up. Sunset from Homer would come down near Augustine Island. I don't see how that would work in a flat earth model. Also there is ham radio on the space station. Hams make contacts with the space station. Hams make contacts with other hams on the ground using radios on the space station. The timing and path those contacts take is predictable and only available when the station is in line of sight as the contacts use VHF radio (usually around 144.8 MHz). Twice a year we have a thing called sun outage. In fact I have to go into work today to switch to a back up satellite for about five minutes while the sun wipes out the signal for AMC1.
